page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 16 shared vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU. The server is equipped with three NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, providing a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning external block storage must be attached for persistent data. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. A notable architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention compared to dedicated CPU instances, though this is offset by the dense memory allocation and dedicated GPU accelerators.

Given the three NVIDIA L4 GPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, this instance is designed for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and parallel processing tasks. The combination of shared vCPUs with high-capacity GPU resources offers a specific resource density profile, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that are heavily dependent on GPU and memory capacity rather than sustained, dedicated host CPU performance.
